long_biography.plain_text:
Raised in Flushing after being born in Brooklyn, Friedmutter studied at Cooper Union and graduated in 1973. Early project-management work introduced him to Henry Conversano, a formative casino designer. Friedmutter then held design-and-construction leadership posts within the resort organisation of Steve Wynn and at Bally's. Those roles taught him to consider operations and customer movement alongside spectacle.

He established his own practice in 1992 and applied that experience to complex entertainment destinations. The business handled projects including The Cosmopolitan, MGM Cotai and Studio City, with assignments spanning buildings, public spaces, restaurants and gaming floors. Its multidisciplinary model turned one architect's specialist knowledge into a durable international professional-services platform, while leaving the underlying resorts in the hands of their developers and operators.
